A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same single-layer, single-gradient unlearning work. All 34 pages of v1 and 30 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIP unlearning measurements in Tables 1–2, layer and multi-identity analyses, and qualitative Stable Diffusion and LLaVA experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Table 1, Table D1, and the main-text and appendix figures. Retained results still qualify as original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The losses, importance/alignment criteria, Pareto layer selection, fixed-gradient update and binary step-size search remain unchanged. Renaming SLSGU to SLUG, expanding joint-update explanations and removing pseudocode do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LAION, CelebA and ImageNet coverage and retain identity, copyrighted-character, object and avocado-chair unlearning scenarios. The additional identities and VLM style-shift examples already appear in v1; moving experiments into appendices adds no coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FT, GA, GAFT, SalUn and SSD with the same comparison membership. The Stable Diffusion comparison in Figure 4 retains SalUn and ESD. The proposed method is renamed, without changing the comparator sets.

E3.justification: v2 Table D1 states that TA excludes the forgotten ImageNet class, whereas v1 Table 2 describes accuracy over all classes. This revises the reported evaluation scope, although values remain identical and v2 also retains an inconsistent 'all classes' sentence. An actual rerun is not established.

E4.justification: The layer-trajectory analysis, joint unlearning of up to six identities, avocado-chair interference example and VLM style-shift cases are retained. v2's new discussion of adversarial recovery and long-term stability supplies limitations, not additional robustness experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for these experiments. Table 1 continues to average over five identities, without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the matched Table 2/Table D1 contain identical numerical results. Corresponding heatmaps, trajectory plots, generated examples and VLM answers are also retained. The revised evaluation wording in Table D1 does not provide changed numerical outcomes.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), including the losses, Fisher-information expression, importance/alignment definitions and update equations, remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs; the removed appendix contains procedural pseudocode.

C1.justification: The central efficiency, selective forgetting, utility-retention and modularity claims remain. v2 additionally claims sequential unlearning in the introduction and strengthens the privacy/copyright framing into an abstract assurance that the method ensures regulatory and intellectual-property compliance, without adding supporting evaluations.

C2.justification: v2 adds a substantial Discussion addressing knowledge localization, practical implications and specific limitations: untested architectures, possible recovery after further training, adversarial recovery and concept granularity. v1 has a short conclusion and narrower case-specific qualifications, including the retained avocado-chair interference explanation.

D1.justification: v2 adds code and data access sections, specific checkpoint links, framework information, and details about generated forget sets and joint step-size searches. Conversely, it removes v1 Appendix F's three algorithms, including explicit initialization, search and final-selection rules. These substantially change the available reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: v2 retains the earlier references and adds MMA-Diffusion, Understanding Neural Networks through Deep Visualization, and Hierarchical Nucleation in Deep Neural Networks. These support expanded misuse and representation-localization discussion, while the central positioning against SalUn and SSD remains.

P1.justification: The title and method name change, the abstract is extensively rewritten, and the introduction and results explanations expand. Background and method sections are consolidated, multi-identity and object experiments move to appendices, and a substantial Discussion replaces the short conclusion.

P2.justification: The paper is globally reformatted with different page geometry, typography and figure sizing. Figures 7–8 and Table 2 move into appendices, captions and diffusion labels expand, Table D1 adds shared-value indicators, and three algorithm displays disappear. The underlying experimental graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves explanation and explicitly acknowledges important generalization, stability and adversarial limitations, while adding reproducibility links. However, it removes detailed algorithm instructions and introduces broader compliance assurances without new evidence. These substantive benefits and harms leave the net quality direction unclear from the PDFs alone.
